title: To Begin the World Again
gist: A 250th-anniversary reappraisal of Thomas Paine separates his durable insights from what the author calls the Enlightenment fallacy — the belief that removing ignorance and prejudice lets reason produce virtue. It argues natural rights exist only insofar as the powerful concede them, credits Paine's Rights of Man and Agrarian Justice as a blueprint that anticipated the 1945 British welfare state, and concludes that America's founding narrative failed because the new world was populated by the same old flawed humans.

themes.theme: Paine as the original mass-persuasion operator

insights.claim: Thomas Paine failed at four careers — corset maker, excise officer, schoolteacher, tobacconist — before Common Sense, a forty-seven-page pamphlet published in January 1776, made him arguably the greatest influencer in American history.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Outsized cultural influence can come from a single short artifact by an otherwise unsuccessful operator — distribution and framing beat credentials.
insights.quote: made him perhaps the greatest “influencer” in our nation’s history
insights.locator: The name of Thomas Paine is far better known

insights.claim: Renaming the pamphlet from its working title Plain Truth to Common Sense, on Benjamin Rush's advice, was a stroke of publishing genius because the title itself pre-loaded readers to treat revolutionary propositions as merely commonsensical.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Framing in the label does persuasive work the argument never has to do — the earliest documented case of naming as a distribution strategy.
insights.locator: Common Sense: But was it? Is it?

insights.claim: Jefferson explicitly stated in a letter to Henry Lee that the Declaration aimed not to find new principles but to place before mankind the common sense of the subject in terms plain enough to command assent, making both founding documents exercises in persuasion rather than discovery.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The founding texts were designed as marketing copy — read them for rhetorical intent, not analytical rigor.
insights.quote: not to find out new principles, or new arguments, never before thought of…; but to place before mankind the common sense of the subject
insights.locator: Common Sense: But was it? Is it?

insights.claim: Paine and Jefferson jointly produced a national myth that remains culturally binding two and a half centuries later even though most of their predictions for the nation failed to come true.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Narratives outlive their predictive track record — durability of a story is uncorrelated with its accuracy.
insights.locator: This is a simplified version of the Enlightenment project

themes.theme: Sorting Paine's common sense from wishful thinking

insights.claim: Paine's structural argument that a continent cannot be perpetually governed by a distant island held, but his corollary that Britain was administratively incapable of governing at that distance was falsified by Britain administering Canada for nearly another century and transitioning it peacefully to self-government.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: A correct directional thesis paired with a wrong mechanism — the standard failure mode of persuasive forecasting.
insights.quote: Britain successfully administered Canada for nearly another century and cooperated peacefully in its eventual shift to self-government.
insights.locator: There were enough judicious and clear-sighted statements

insights.claim: Paine's portrayal of George III as the hardened, sullen-tempered Pharaoh of England was propaganda rather than description, since Andrew Roberts's biography shows George worked within the constitutional settlement of 1688 and never sought a return to autocracy.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The villain in a founding narrative was manufactured — a caution against accepting the antagonist any movement supplies.
insights.quote: as cultured, civilized, enlightened, and good-natured a monarch as it is possible to find in European history
insights.locator: All very well, and most believers

insights.claim: The clearest proof George III was not a tyrant is procedural: an actual tyrant would not have allowed the Continental Congresses to assemble, and would have arrested and hanged the Revolution's ringleaders including Paine, whereas the policy toward Paine after the seditious Rights of Man was permanent exile rather than punishment.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Test claims of tyranny against what the accused regime permitted, not against what its opponents said about it.
insights.locator: All very well, and most believers

insights.claim: Paine's aphorism that whichever power in the constitution has the most weight will govern is his most durable prediction, playing out visibly in contemporary American politics.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Formal constitutional design matters less than where actual weight sits — the operative question in any institutional-power analysis.
insights.quote: it only remains to know which power in the constitution has the most weight, for that will govern
insights.locator: Paine said some remarkably prescient things

insights.claim: Paine's proposition that perfect equality affords no temptation has been refuted by 250 years of representative government, though formal equality before the law remains a reasonable and sometimes achievable goal.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Distinguishes the achievable target (legal equality) from the utopian one (outcome equality) — a live distinction in any redistribution debate.
insights.quote: there can be no superiority, perfect equality affords no temptation
insights.locator: Paine said some remarkably prescient things

insights.claim: The Enlightenment fallacy is the belief that evil is merely error produced by ignorance, which forces rationalists to explain persistent human darkness by inventing sinister interests — wicked priests, profiteers, malignant enemies of enlightenment.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: A reusable diagnostic: when a worldview cannot account for opposition except through conspiracy, it has inherited a theology it claims to have discarded.
insights.quote: Modern rationalists reject the idea of evil while being obsessed by it. Seeing themselves as embattled warriors in a struggle against darkness, it has not occurred to them to ask why humankind is so fond of the dark.
insights.locator: If there is an Enlightenment project

insights.claim: The 1789 Declaration of the Rights of Man encoded the Enlightenment fallacy in its opening sentence by naming ignorance, neglect, or contempt of human rights as the sole causes of public misfortunes and governmental corruption.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
entities: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
insights.so_what: Monocausal explanations of political failure were baked into the founding documents of the modern order and still shape reform assumptions.
insights.quote: ignorance, neglect, or contempt of human rights, are the sole causes of public misfortunes and corruptions of Government
insights.locator: It is an illusion that informed

insights.claim: Optimism, not accuracy, determines political reach: Jefferson and Paine outcompeted Adams and Madison because hope is a potent message, the same dynamic that made 'Yes, we can' work in 2008.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Persistent structural advantage for optimistic political messaging regardless of its empirical basis — expect hope to keep beating realism at the ballot box.
insights.quote: Hope is always a potent political message; indeed, inspirational leadership is hardly possible in its absence.
insights.locator: It is an illusion that informed

insights.claim: Paine's claim that reason obeys itself while ignorance submits is contradicted by the fact that some of the most highly educated people in the world have followed insane creeds as meekly as sheep.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Education is not a defense against ideological capture — undercuts the assumption that better-informed populations are more resistant to manipulation.
insights.quote: some of the most highly educated people in the world have followed insane creeds as meekly as sheep
insights.locator: The sole causes? Really?

insights.claim: Paine's premise that mankind is always ripe enough to understand its true interest if presented clearly collapses in a fractured mediascape where the public cannot adjudicate among competing explicators, none of whom is free of self-design.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The information-abundance problem is structural, not new — it was already visible in the pamphlet era and has only compounded.
insights.quote: In today’s fractured mediascape, it has become nearly impossible.
insights.locator: The sole causes? Really?

themes.theme: Natural rights are contingent on power

insights.claim: There is good reason to doubt natural rights actually exist: they appear real only where those in power choose to govern as if they do, which means rights are what those in power allow.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Treat rights as a revocable political settlement rather than a fixed floor — the practical framing when assessing regime risk.
insights.quote: Rights are what those in power allow.
insights.locator: Again, is this “common sense” or wishful thinking?

insights.claim: Enlightenment natural rights were grounded in a benign deity, Jefferson's 'Nature's God,' so as belief declines the modern basis for rights must fall back on idealism, decency, goodwill and innate altruism — qualities too often insufficient to limit greed or check the will to power.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Secularization removes the original load-bearing justification for rights without supplying an equally strong replacement — a slow structural vulnerability.
insights.locator: But in the years since Paine wrote

insights.claim: Paine and Burke were each half right: Paine underestimated elites' determination to keep privileges and the strength of habitual obedience, while Burke failed to see that the monarchy he revered was doomed by the two Declarations.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Both the idealist and the reactionary misprice the same variable — the persistence of existing power — in opposite directions.
insights.quote: in his consistently underestimating both the determination of monarchs and aristocrats to retain their privileges and the strength of the habit of obedience which secured them the loyalty even of those whom they oppressed.
insights.locator: The Rights of Man was written as a retort

insights.claim: Burke, previously an ally of the left who opposed British repression of the American colonists, broke with Paine by dismissing the Declaration of the Rights of Man as paltry and blurred shreds of paper, and his cynicism about people's willingness to be led was very often justified.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
entities: Reflections on the Revolution in France
insights.so_what: The conservative critique of revolutionary rights talk has a better empirical record than its reputation suggests.
insights.quote: paltry and blurred shreds of paper about the rights of men
insights.locator: The Rights of Man was written as a retort

insights.claim: The exclusion of women and enslaved people from the Declarations is a weak basis for deriding their authors, because the documents inspired movements that led inevitably to extending rights to those groups.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
entities: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
insights.so_what: Judge founding texts by the trajectory they set in motion rather than by their point-in-time scope.
insights.locator: The Declaration of Independence and the Declaration

insights.claim: Paine's strongest work is Part II of The Rights of Man and Part I of Agrarian Justice (1797), where he laid out a functioning social welfare state — pensions for the elderly, grants for newlyweds and young people, funeral costs, universal education, progressive but not onerous taxation, a public works program, and collective bargaining rights.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The full modern welfare architecture was specified in 1791–1797, which reframes it as a founding-era idea rather than a twentieth-century import.
insights.locator: Paine’s finest moment, I think

insights.claim: Paine's program is in fact very close to what the British Labour government introduced in 1945, with health care absent only because no health care system existed in his day.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: A 150-year lag between blueprint and implementation — policy ideas can sit fully formed for generations before political conditions permit them.
insights.quote: His program is in fact very close to what the British Labour government introduced in 1945.
insights.locator: Those who complain about lazy welfare recipients

insights.claim: Paine framed social security as a right rather than a charity, and framed education as a right on the grounds that only monarchical and aristocratical government requires ignorance for its support.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The rights-versus-charity framing is the original argument structure still used in every entitlement fight.
insights.quote: is not of the nature of a charity, but of a right
insights.locator: Those who complain about lazy welfare recipients

insights.claim: The Iraq invasion and occupation cost, inflation-adjusted, thirteen times as much as the entire Marshall Plan — roughly two trillion dollars that would have more than paid for every social welfare expense Paine proposed.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: A concrete opportunity-cost benchmark for the guns-versus-welfare tradeoff in US fiscal allocation.
insights.quote: cost—after adjustment for inflation—thirteen times as much as the entire Marshall Plan
insights.locator: Those who complain about lazy welfare recipients

insights.claim: Paine's test for a legitimate constitution — poor are happy, jails empty of prisoners, streets empty of beggars, the aged not in want, taxes not oppressive — remains unmet, and Bernie Sanders beats the same drum 250 years later with about as much success.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The redistributive argument has been stable and unsuccessful for two and a half centuries — low base rate for it succeeding now.
insights.quote: Bernie Sanders still beats the same drum Paine did two and a half centuries on, and with about as much success.
insights.locator: It hardly needs to be pointed out

insights.claim: Enlightened republicanism delivered not equality and virtue but a dog-eat-dog society of competitive radical individualism, a divergence Paine lived to see before dying nearly penniless in 1809.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The founding project's actual output diverged from its stated goal within a single generation — a base rate worth applying to any institutional design promise.
insights.quote: Enlightened republicanism had ushered in not equality and virtue but a dog-eat-dog society of competitive and radical individualism.
insights.locator: Paine wagered all on the virtue

insights.claim: Hamilton observed contemporaneously that preaching the necessity of disinterestedness in republics fails to make a single proselyte, confirming that the civic-virtue premise was known to be failing by the founders themselves.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Insider skepticism about civic virtue is as old as the republic — the disillusionment is not a modern development.
insights.quote: We may preach till we are tired of the theme, the necessity of disinterestedness in republics, without making a single proselyte.
insights.locator: Paine wagered all on the virtue

insights.claim: Paine's move to Paris in 1792 and his seat in the National Convention ended with him imprisoned in the Luxembourg Palace during the Terror, personally witnessing how leveling revolutions consume their own champions and validating all of Burke's forebodings.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The canonical case study in revolutionary reflexivity — the architect of the theory becomes its casualty.
insights.locator: Paine wagered all on the virtue

insights.claim: Paine believed the ignorant mob was an artifact of Europe's bad old regimes that would disappear under representative government, and would never have imagined that self-serving grifters could be elected to high office.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Names the specific falsified assumption — that governance form would upgrade the governed — underlying democratic optimism.
insights.locator: It was not at all what the Founders had planned

insights.claim: A historical comparison between monarchs and elected leaders does not indicate a general superiority of one group over the other, vindicating Abbé Sieyès's suggestion that Paine dismissed as inadmissible.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Selection mechanism matters less than assumed for leader quality — a direct challenge to a core democratic-legitimacy claim.
insights.locator: It was not at all what the Founders had planned

insights.claim: Paine was right that a new world was at hand, but there were no new-model humans to populate it, so the nation can only be as virtuous as the all-too-human material it is made of.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The binding constraint on institutional reform is human nature, not institutional design — discount projections that assume otherwise.
insights.quote: there were no new-model humans to populate the new world, only the same old flawed, imperfectible animals
insights.locator: “We have it in our power to begin the world over again,”

insights.claim: Much of what Paine hated about eighteenth-century Britain now describes the United States: extreme social and economic inequality, compromised elections, abrogated rights, an overweening executive, unfettered warmongering, and imperial overreach.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: The revolutionary indictment has rotated onto the successor state — a framing increasingly common in mainstream American cultural criticism.
insights.locator: This is a simplified version of the Enlightenment project
